column1: # One row per message that pg_sift sends to the client at NOTICE, WARNING or INFO: what scripts/gen-messages.sh reads, with the emitters of src/ and sql/, to check the rows and to write docs/MESSAGES.md.

# A new message needs a row (scripts/gen-messages.sh --skeleton prints it with the text, level, DETAIL and HINT filled in); a message that is reworded or removed changes or removes its row in the same commit.

# id: a lowercase slug, the anchor of the row in docs/MESSAGES.md. group: create, limits, maint, planning or upgrade (the sections of the page). level: NOTICE, WARNING or INFO (the level a VACUUM VERBOSE report is raised at).

# source: the C file that raises the message, or the first SQL script of a released path that does. message, detail, hint: the literal of the errmsg, errdetail and errhint of the source (RAISE .. USING of the SQL), %s and %d as written;
#   checked against the source. A detail or hint the source builds at run time is checked only when it is one literal.

# fires: the statement or operation. when: the condition, in plain words. decision: what pg_sift chose by itself (None for an advice). switch: the option, setting or command that changes or switches it off, and its default.

# title, default, gain, cost: the row of the "Decisions at a glance" table (all four, or none for a message that is not a decision); gain and cost are short. benefit, tradeoff: the full figures with their conditions.

# Every number of gain, cost, benefit and tradeoff is quoted: it must be in a row of docs/options.tsv named in `option` (comma separated keys) or in a file of `evidence` (comma separated paths); a cell without a number says "no measured number yet" or "n/a: reason".
# doc: file#heading of docs/ for the longer explanation.
# kind, choice, why, off: a row with a kind is one line of the summary that CREATE INDEX and REINDEX print and of sift.index_choices(index), derived from the finished index by src/col/build/choices.c

#   (no emitter of its own, and its message, detail and hint are not a source literal). auto: a choice the index holds; advice: a suggestion; limit: where a cap left units without what was asked; action: something to do

#   (a row that is also raised where the source says, like track-changes-concurrent, keeps its message, detail and hint). choice: the name in the summary; why: one plain sentence, 100 characters at most, no number that is not measured;

#   off: the command that turns it off, %s the index name. sift.help(id) returns the row. docs/messages-length.allow lists the older cells over the length limit (first line 100 characters, detail 200, hint 100, no ".." shorthand).
